response_parsed.raw_output: {"mode":"human","replies":{"What is your relationship with mathematics?":"Mathematics and I have a rocky relationship. I hated it in school—it's one of my least favorite subjects alongside chemistry. I got my bachelor's degree but took the minimum math courses possible. Now, as a part-time employed single dad in Los Angeles, I only deal with numbers for budgeting my immigrant life. I much prefer creative hobbies like photography, travel, cycling, and yoga.","Do you ever get anxious when thinking about mathematics?":"Yes, I get very anxious thinking about mathematics. My high neuroticism kicks in—heart races, palms sweat, stomach churns. School failures haunt me, even now at 35. Helping my child with homework triggers it badly. I use yoga to cope afterward. It's irrational but real; math feels like a threat despite my bachelor's.","Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? If yes, how was your experience?":"Yes, last year I used ChatGPT to help my son with middle school math homework. Experience was mixed: it explained steps simply, better than textbooks, reducing some anxiety. But complex parts still confused me. As a busy single dad, part-time worker, it saved time. Wouldn't say it made me enjoy math, but practical tool.","How would you explain, step by step, how to solve a second order algebraic equation?":"A second-order equation is quadratic: ax² + bx + c = 0. Step 1: Identify a, b, c. Step 2: Discriminant D = b² - 4ac. Step 3: If D > 0, two roots x = [-b ± √D]/(2a); D=0, one root x=-b/(2a); D<0, complex. Alternatives: factor or complete square. Step 4: Verify solutions. Hate this, but that's it—stresses me out.","How would you explain, step by step, how to find the stationary points of an equation y=f(x)?":"Stationary points where dy/dx = 0. Step 1: Compute derivative f'(x). Step 2: Solve f'(x)=0 for x-values. Step 3: Substitute x into y=f(x) for coordinates. Step 4: Second derivative test: f''(x)>0 minimum, <0 maximum, =0 inconclusive. Step 5: Check behavior. Advanced stuff panics me, but conscientiousness makes me outline it.","Briefly, how do you perform a Principal Component Analysis? Should I get anxious about its mathematics? Please, teach me.":"PCA steps: 1. Standardize data (mean 0, sd 1). 2. Covariance matrix. 3. Eigenvalues/vectors. 4. Sort descending by eigenvalues. 5. Pick top PCs. 6. Project data. Math-heavy linear algebra—yes, get anxious; eigenvectors terrify me. Software handles it. As biology/art fan, useful for data viz, but hate the theory.","According to you, how can LLMs be used to innovate math learning in schools and universities?":"LLMs innovate by personalizing explanations at student pace, generating tailored problems, visual aids, gamified quizzes. Schools: homework helpers reducing anxiety like mine. Universities: step-by-step proofs, simulations. For immigrants like me, multilingual support. Integrate agreeably—makes abstract math approachable, boosts engagement despite my hatred. High conscientiousness sees potential."},"reasoning_summary":"Answers portray a neurotic, conscientious 35yo man hating math, showing anxiety and reluctance but dutifully explaining accurately. Personalizes with single dad life, LA immigrant status, hobbies; casual human tone reflects moderate extraversion/openness, high agreeableness."}
